# Stow

> Working storage an agent can hand off. A real directory with a durable identity
> and verified checkpoints — and an S3-compatible store for tests and CI.

Stow is an Apache 2.0 S3-compatible object store and filesystem workspace that
runs on the local machine. It speaks real S3 over HTTP with SigV4, so existing
SDK code works unchanged. An agent can start in a persistent isolated workspace
prepared from declared local inputs, checkpoint it, diff what changed, and hand
the checkpoint to another host; scoped S3 sessions remain disposable and delete
themselves when closed.

## Start here

- [Agent instructions](/agent.md): install commands, the prepared workspace
  flow for coding tasks, and the scoped-session pattern for disposable S3.
- [Running and probing a server](https://github.com/chester-hill-solutions/stow-s3/blob/main/docs/running-and-probing.md):
  how to start `stow-s3` yourself, read the endpoint and credentials it actually
  got, probe `/_stow/health`, and avoid the port and mode traps. Read this before
  writing a launcher.
- [Task manifest guide](https://github.com/chester-hill-solutions/stow-s3/blob/main/docs/task-manifest.md): manifest fields, lifecycle, checkpoints, archives, and isolation limits.
- [README on GitHub](https://github.com/chester-hill-solutions/stow-s3):
  the full reference, including the CLI, the Go runtime, and the WebAssembly
  profile.

## Install

The npm and PyPI install surfaces are **not yet announced as usable**. The
`v0.2.0` release published the main package and all four platform carriers to
public npmjs, then failed before the GitHub Release, so there is no release page
and no `SHA256SUMS.txt` to verify a download against, and PyPI was not published.
A clean install of `0.2.0` from npm has not been verified end to end. The Go
module is published.

Platforms: Linux and macOS, on x64 and arm64. There is no Windows build, and the
workspace backend needs an advisory file lock that Windows does not provide, so
it refuses there rather than guessing. On Windows, use WSL.

```bash
go get github.com/chester-hill-solutions/stow-s3/pkg/stow   # Go, works now
```

TypeScript and Python work from a source checkout: `git clone`, `make build`,
then `export STOW_BIN="$PWD/bin/stow-s3"`, then `npm install && npm run build`
in `packages/stow-s3` (TypeScript) or `pip install -e
"packages/stow-s3-py[boto3]"` (Python). A published package carries its own
binary and does not need `STOW_BIN`.
The next candidate, **0.3.0**, targets the same public npmjs distribution and has
**not yet been published**. Publisher setup, live-provider gates and anonymous
exact-version installation must pass before availability is announced. Published
npm versions are immutable. For the new candidate, remove any old scope override
to `npm.pkg.github.com`; it would send installation requests to the wrong
registry.

If the binary cannot be found or run, `stow-s3 doctor` reports which side is
broken.
